Balanced training/testing split

Source: R/balanced_initial_split.R
balanced_initial_split.Rd

balanced_initial_split() makes one training/testing split in which the two sets are similar on several variables at once. Use rsample::training() and rsample::testing() to get the two data sets.

Usage

balanced_initial_split(
  data,
  prop = 3/4,
  balance = NULL,
  exact = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  method = "anticlust",
  options = list(),
  na = "error",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

prop

The proportion of data (or of groups, if you use group) for the training set. With method = "twinning", prop must be 1 - 1/r or 1/r for a whole number r, for example 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 9/10, or 1/4. Write it as a fraction such as 2 / 3, not a rounded decimal such as 0.67. A value within a relative 1e-8 of such a fraction counts as that fraction.

balance

<tidy-select> Columns to balance across the sets. Numeric columns are standardized. So are Date, POSIXct, and difftime columns, as numbers of days or seconds. Factor, character, and logical columns become one indicator column per level.

exact

<tidy-select> Categorical columns to stratify exactly. Each combination of levels is one stratum. In each stratum, the count in every set is the floor or the ceiling of its proportional share, based on the actual size of that set. For folds, the counts of a stratum also differ by at most one over the folds whenever both rules can hold at once. With group, these counts are numbers of groups, not rows. exact does the job of strata in rsample, but it takes several columns and its counts are exact. Numeric columns with whole-number values are treated as categories. Put continuous columns in balance, or use cut() to make a factor if you need exact counts within ranges. A stratum whose share of the smallest set is under one row (or group) can be missing from some sets. If more than half of the strata are missing from at least one set, you get a warning.

group

<tidy-select> One column with group IDs. All rows of a group go to the same set. See Details.

method

The balancing method: "anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", or "interaction". See Details.

options

A named list of options for the method. See Details.

na

What to do with missing values in the balance and exact columns. "error" (the default) stops with an error. "include" balances on which values are missing; see Missing values. The group column must not have missing values either way.

...

Not used. Must be empty.

Value

An rsplit object with class balanced_initial_split and initial_split.

Details

The methods, options, and group handling are the same as for balanced_vfold_cv(). With method = "twinning", the split uses twinning::twin(), and the options are leaf_size only. Strata with fewer than 2 * r rows (or groups) are split at random.

If a workflow has a postprocessor that must be trained, tune::last_fit() splits the training set again with balanced_initial_split(), using the same arguments.

See also

balanced_vfold_cv(), balance_check()

Examples

set.seed(1)
split <- balanced_initial_split(
  sim_patients,
  prop = 3 / 4,
  balance = c(age, income),
  exact = c(diagnosis, site)
)
split
#> # Balanced training/testing split (anticlust), balancing age, income,
#> # stratified by diagnosis, site
#> <Training/Testing/Total>
#> <225/75/300>
head(rsample::training(split))
#>        age    income diagnosis site  outcome
#> 1 45.41686 10059.820      none    A 4.869271
#> 2 23.63934  8132.757      none    C 5.043892
#> 3 45.00346 31997.909      none    C 4.053658
#> 4 56.92559 22235.349      mild    B 8.176950
#> 5 28.47077 14181.133      mild    C 3.617587
#> 6 27.86498  7221.059      none    A 4.605030
